column1: # Linkage freezes that a consumer may read INSTEAD of the one the manifest
# describes -- each with the hash it expects and why reading it is legitimate.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. verify_linkage_freeze() used to accept any hash at all
# through the ALLOW_FREEZE_SHA256 environment variable: ambient, invisible to
# code review, applying to every consumer in the process, and leaving no record
# of which freeze was read or on whose authority. That is the mechanism by which
# a build came to describe 11,920 midwives instead of 12,171 (docs/DATA_VAULT.md).
# A deliberate pin is still allowed -- it has to be written down here first.
# A pin is NOT a licence to publish. Nothing in this file may back a cohort
# count, a table or a figure in the manuscript; those come from the freeze the
# tracked manifest names, and nothing else. A pin exists so that a dated
# experiment stays reproducible against the data it actually scored.
# Columns: sha256  consumer  rows  members  scope  doc  purpose
#   consumer = the ONE script this pin is for. A pin does not carry over to any
#           other script: keying on the hash alone would mean that unlocking a
#           freeze for one dated experiment unlocks it for every consumer in the
#           repository, published counts included.
#   scope = experiment | historical    (never "production": production IS the
#           manifest's freeze, which needs no pin)
# Delete a row when its consumer stops reading that freeze -- a pin must not
# outlive its cause.
